name: Waseda University
summary: Private Tokyo university founded in 1882; six schools teach full English-based bachelor's degrees, with September entry and no Japanese to apply.

ib.text: Predicted IB grades are accepted and no minimum score is set; 2026 successful applicants averaged 36.4 to 38.9 of 42 by school. An English test (TOEFL iBT or IELTS) is needed unless the guide exempts you.

apply.via: Waseda's online system (TAO), one application per school

dates.label: Results announced: Political Science and Economics
Results announced: Science and Engineering schools (final)

programmes.name: Political Science and Economics
programmes.about: Three English-taught degrees in one school: Political Science, Economics, and Global Political Economy, which splits coursework evenly between the two. Small discussion seminars of 5 to 15 students run throughout.
programmes.selectionNote: Holistic review of IB grades, English test, essay and recommendation; interview only if invited. About 100 places. Choose one of the three degrees at application.

programmes.name: Transnational and Interdisciplinary Studies in Social Innovation (TAISI)
programmes.about: An English-based programme in the School of Social Sciences that trains students as social innovators and agents of change, approaching global issues across disciplines. It awards a BA in Social Sciences.
programmes.selectionNote: Holistic review of IB grades, English test, a 1,000-word statement of purpose and recommendation; interview if invited. About 60 places; a May round runs only if conducted.

programmes.name: International Liberal Studies
programmes.about: A broad liberal-arts degree taught in English, set up in 2004, for students who want to range across fields. You choose Study Plan 1 or 2 by language background; Plan 1 includes a compulsory year abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: Holistic review of the documents; interviews on 26 or 27 March 2027 for some applicants. About 150 places, about 70 of them in the first window.

programmes.name: Global Studies in Japanese Cultures Program (JCulP)
programmes.about: English-taught study of Japanese culture in all its diversity, with a focus on Japanese literature, alongside Japanese students in Tokyo. It awards a BA in Literature.
programmes.ib: Needs TOEFL iBT 95 or IELTS 7.0 (or an accepted equivalent) as a minimum; applications below it are not accepted.
programmes.selectionNote: Holistic review of IB grades, English score and an essay of around 800 words. Only 15 places in the overseas-students category (23 of 162 applicants admitted in 2026).

programmes.name: Fundamental Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Two English-taught majors: Mathematical Sciences, from the fundamentals of science to specialist mathematical theory, and Computer Science and Communications Engineering. Flexible minors are possible.
programmes.ib: Your IB results must cover maths, physics and chemistry; the interview can test all three.
programmes.selectionNote: Document screening, then an interview that may cover maths, physics and chemistry. About 30 places per school. Choose one major at application.

separateFrom.name: Creative Science and Engineering
separateFrom.reason: A separate school with its own majors (mechanical, civil and environmental engineering), though it shares one application guide and window.

programmes.name: Creative Science and Engineering
programmes.about: Two English-taught engineering majors, Mechanical Engineering and Civil and Environmental Engineering, with a curriculum from general engineering courses to specialised theory and practice.
programmes.ib: Your IB results must cover maths, physics and chemistry; the interview can test all three.
programmes.selectionNote: Document screening, then an interview that may cover maths, physics and chemistry. About 30 places per school. Choose one major at application.

separateFrom.name: Fundamental Science and Engineering
separateFrom.reason: A separate school with its own majors (mathematical sciences, computer science and communications), though it shares one application guide and window.

notes: Waseda gives merit scholarships at admission with no separate application; they are partial, and none covers full costs.
Predicted IB grades are used for the decision; successful applicants must later submit final IB results, so ask the school office for that date.
Tuition is shown without the one-off ¥200,000 registration fee; lab, library and association fees come on top each year.
